questions.question: 'Statistical averages must be used with caution'. Comment.
questions.solution_html:
• Statistical averages must be used with caution because they can hide crucial variations
  • within the data, be easily skewed by extreme values, and provide a misleading
  • representation of the entire situation if the data is not normally distributed.
  • Averages are designed for quantitative data. Calculating an "average" for
  • qualitative characteristics (like honesty or intelligence) or categorical data (like
  • the average number of wheels on different types of vehicles) can result in a
  • meaningless or absurd figure
  • Averages only show a midpoint and not the entire range or spread of results
  • Statistical conclusions are only as good as the data they are based on.
  • (Consider any relevant point- 4 points + explanation)
  • 20 117 582

questions.question: Given μ ₂ =9, μ ₃ =0, μ ₄ =200, analyze skewness and kurtosis.
questions.solution_html:
• Skewness ( 3.5 marks with interpretation)
  • β₁ = μ₃² / μ₂³ = 0² / 9³ = 0 / 729 = 0
  • Since β₁ = 0 (γ₁ = 0), the distribution is symmetrical — there is no skewness.
  • Kurtosis ( 3.5 marks with interpretation)
  • β₂ = μ₄ / μ₂² = 200 / 9² = 200 / 81 = 2.47 (approx.)
  • Since β₂ = 2.47 is less than 3 (γ₂ = β₂ − 3 = −0.53, negative), the distribution is platykurtic

questions.question: Distinguish between Census Method and Sampling Method.
questions.solution_html:
• Coverage: Census covers every unit of the population; Sampling covers only a representative
  • Cost: Census is more expensive as it covers the entire population; Sampling is more
  • economical.
  • Time: Census takes a longer time to complete; Sampling is quicker.
  • Accuracy: Census, in principle, gives more accurate/complete results (subject to non
  • sampling errors); Sampling results are subject to sampling error but can be highly accurate
  • with proper design.
  • Suitability: Census is suitable for small, homogeneous, or when data on every unit is legally
  • required (e.g., population census); Sampling is suitable for large populations and destructive
  • testing.
  • Manpower/Resources: Census requires a larger organisation and manpower; Sampling
  • requires comparatively fewer resources.
